verses.text: Faith means being sure of what we hope for, and certain of what we cannot see.
It was because of their faith that God was pleased with people long ago.
By faith we understand that God made the universe by his word. So what we see was not made out of things that can be seen.

By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. Because of his faith, God said he was a good man, and God accepted his gifts. Even though Abel is dead, he still speaks to us through his faith.
By faith Enoch was taken up to God without dying. No one could find him, because God had taken him away. Before he was taken, Scripture says that he pleased God.
Without faith, no one can please God. Anyone who comes to God must believe that he is real, and that he rewards those who look for him.

By faith Noah built a big boat to save his family. God warned him about things that had not yet happened, and he honoured God and obeyed. By his faith he showed the world was wrong, and he became one of those whom God accepts because of their faith.
By faith Abraham obeyed when God called him to go to a land he would later receive as his own. He left, even though he did not know where he was going.
By faith he lived like a foreigner in the land God had promised him. He lived in tents, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who received the same promise.
Abraham was waiting for the city with lasting foundations, the city planned and built by God.
By faith even Sarah was able to have a child, though she was too old. She trusted that God would keep his promise.
So from one man, who was as good as dead, came a family as many as the stars in the sky, and as many as the grains of sand on the seashore, which no one can count.

All these people were still living by faith when they died. They did not receive what God had promised, but they saw it coming from far away and welcomed it. They said that they were only strangers and visitors on earth.
People who say things like that show that they are looking for a home of their own.
If they had been thinking about the country they had left, they could have gone back.
Instead, they wanted a better country, a home in heaven. So God is not ashamed to be called their God, because he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham offered Isaac as a sacrifice when God tested him. Abraham had received God's promises, yet he was ready to offer his only son.
God had told him, "Your family line will come through Isaac."
Abraham believed that God could even raise the dead. And in a way, he did get Isaac back from death.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, speaking about their future.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons. He worshipped God as he leaned on the top of his walking stick.
By faith Joseph, when he was about to die, spoke about the people of Israel leaving Egypt. He told them what to do with his bones.
By faith Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born. They saw he was a special child, and they were not afraid of the king's order.
By faith Moses, when he grew up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
He chose to suffer with God's people rather than enjoy the pleasures of sin for a short time.
He thought that being insulted for the sake of Christ was worth more than all the treasures of Egypt, because he was looking ahead to his reward.
By faith Moses left Egypt, and he was not afraid of the king's anger. He kept going because he saw God, who cannot be seen.
By faith Moses kept the Passover, and had blood sprinkled on the doorposts, so that the angel who killed the firstborn would not touch the firstborn of Israel.
By faith the people walked through the Red Sea as if on dry land. When the Egyptians tried to follow, they drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
By faith Rahab, the prostitute, was not killed with those who disobeyed God, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
What more can I say? I do not have time to tell you about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets.
Through faith they defeated kingdoms, did what was right, and received what God promised. They shut the mouths of lions,
put out raging fires, and escaped being killed by the sword. They were weak, but they were made strong. They became powerful in battle and chased away foreign armies.
Women received their loved ones back from death. Others were tortured and refused to be set free, so that they would rise to a better life.
Some were laughed at and beaten with whips. Others were put in chains and thrown into prison.

Some were killed with stones, some were cut in two, and some were tempted. Some were killed with the sword. Some wandered around wearing the skins of sheep and goats. They were poor, suffering and treated badly.
The world was not good enough for them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and lived in caves and holes in the ground.
God was pleased with all of them because of their faith, but none of them received what God had promised.
God had planned something better that includes us, so that they would only be made perfect together with us.
